newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S., Japan, S.Korea officials begin N.Korea talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Japan, S.Korea officials begin N.Korea talks.

text.p: The United States, Japan and South Korea began talks in Tokyo on Wednesday to coordinate policies on troubled North Korea.
The one-day discussions at the Japanese Foreign Ministry are to focus on food shortages in the North and ways to encourage the Stalinist nation to join peace talks, South Korean officials said.

The trilateral discussions are led by Charles Kartman, U.S. deputy assistant secretary of state, Yu Myung-hwan, director-general for North American affairs at the South Korean Foreign Ministry, and his Japanese counterpart, Ryozo Kato.
Peace talks involving the two Koreas, the United States and China are aimed at closing the book on the 1950-53 Korean War, which ended in a now-fraying armistice.
At talks in New York two weeks ago, the United States and South Korea failed to get North Korea to join Korean peninsula peace negotiations.
Washington and Seoul have said substantial aid to North Korea could be discussed during peace talks, although humanitarian assistance would be provided to help stave off a catastrophe.
On Tuesday, Catherine Bertini,the director of the World Food Programme, appealed to governments to give food aid directly to North Korea because her agency could not handle all emergency needs.
The World Food Programme, a United Nations agency, so far this year has appealed for 200,000 tonnes of food for North Korea, or about $95 million. About $38.6 million of this has been raised.
The United States has pledged $25 million and South Korea $6 million.
Japan has held back food aid, partly due to anger over charges that North Korea kidnapped a Japanese schoolgirl in 1977 and spirited her to Pyongyang.
